root_cause.text: The bounds check in `check_xattrs()` only verifies that the next xattr entry pointer starts before the `end` boundary, failing to ensure there is sufficient space (at least 4 bytes) to safely execute the `IS_LAST_ENTRY()` macro on the subsequent iteration.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff replaces the check `if ((void *)next >= end)` with `if ((void *)next + sizeof(u32) > end)` in `fs/ext4/xattr.c`, and the description notes that "if next lands at end - 1, the check passes since next < end, but IS_LAST_ENTRY() reads 4 bytes starting at end - 1, accessing 3 bytes beyond the valid region."

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `check_xattrs` contains the vulnerable bounds check on lines 228-231: `if ((void *)next >= end)`. This check only ensures that the pointer `next` starts before `end`, but does not verify that there are at least 4 bytes (the size of the entry's header checked by `IS_LAST_ENTRY`) remaining before `end`. On the subsequent iteration, `IS_LAST_ENTRY(e)` will dereference `e` (which is `next`), potentially causing an out-of-bounds read if `next` is within 4 bytes of `end`.
